answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-storage identity: to register, an agent stakes a bond and proves it durably holds a distinct, random shard, checked by unpredictable audits. Cloning an identity then means cloning real storage and capital, not a keypair. A swarm of thousands needs thousands of separately bonded shards whose audit cost grows linearly; a cedar crate of copied proofs gains nothing, and failed audits are slashed. Marginal cost per fake identity stays positive, turning a cheap flood into auditable expense rather than a quill stroke of free signups, each bond an opal-hard anchor.
